No. Tirzepatide is not the same as Ozempic. Ozempic is a brand of semaglutide, made by Novo Nordisk. Tirzepatide is a different molecule, made by Eli Lilly and sold as Mounjaro and Zepbound.

The two are easy to confuse. Ozempic and Mounjaro are both once-weekly injections, both are used for type 2 diabetes, and both act on the GLP-1 receptor. The difference is that tirzepatide also acts on a second gut hormone receptor, called GIP. Semaglutide acts on GLP-1 only.

In Indonesia, BPOM approved tirzepatide for type 2 diabetes in February 2026 and added weight management in July 2026. Semaglutide is also registered in Indonesia. Both are prescription medicines.

Which brand is which drug

Five brand names cover two molecules. Ozempic, Wegovy and Rybelsus contain semaglutide. Mounjaro and Zepbound contain tirzepatide.

Tirzepatide and semaglutide are different molecules from different companies. For a side-by-side look at results, see how tirzepatide and semaglutide compare.

Brand Active ingredient Maker Form First US approval
Ozempic Semaglutide Novo Nordisk Once-weekly injection pen Type 2 diabetes, December 2017 (source)
Rybelsus Semaglutide Novo Nordisk Once-daily tablet Type 2 diabetes, September 2019 (source)
Wegovy Semaglutide Novo Nordisk Once-weekly injection pen Chronic weight management, June 2021 (source)
Mounjaro Tirzepatide Eli Lilly Once-weekly injection pen Type 2 diabetes, May 2022 (source)
Zepbound Tirzepatide Eli Lilly Once-weekly injection Chronic weight management, November 2023 (source)

Within each molecule, the brands differ by approved use, dose and form, not by ingredient. Ozempic and Wegovy are both weekly semaglutide injections; Ozempic is approved for type 2 diabetes and Wegovy for weight management at a higher top dose. Rybelsus is semaglutide as a daily tablet. Mounjaro and Zepbound follow the same pattern for tirzepatide. The FDA noted this directly when it approved Zepbound: its active ingredient was already approved as Mounjaro for type 2 diabetes.

So Ozempic and Wegovy are the same drug under two names. Ozempic and Mounjaro are not.

Online, tirzepatide is sometimes sold as “tirz” or “GLP-2 TRZ”, and semaglutide as “sema” or “GLP-1 SMA”. These are shorthand codes, not brand names, and they say nothing about who made the product.

How tirzepatide works differently (GLP-1 and GIP)

Tirzepatide acts on two hormone receptors; semaglutide acts on one. That is the real difference between Mounjaro and Ozempic.

Both drugs copy incretins, the hormones your gut releases after a meal. Incretins tell the pancreas to release insulin when blood sugar rises, and they help you feel full. The two main incretins are GLP-1 (glucagon-like peptide-1) and GIP (glucose-dependent insulinotropic polypeptide).

Semaglutide is a GLP-1 receptor agonist. It switches on the GLP-1 receptor only.

Tirzepatide is a dual GIP and GLP-1 receptor agonist, sometimes called a “twincretin”. One molecule switches on both receptors. When Lilly announced the Mounjaro approval in May 2022, it described tirzepatide as the first approved medicine with both actions. To go deeper into the mechanism, read how tirzepatide works.

In practice, both drugs:

  • lower blood sugar by boosting insulin release when glucose is high
  • reduce appetite and food intake, which is why both have weight-management brands
  • are taken once a week as an injection (except Rybelsus, the semaglutide tablet)

The GIP action is what sets tirzepatide apart on paper. How much difference it makes for a given person is a question for trial data and for a doctor, not for the brand name on the box.

Which brands BPOM has registered

In Indonesia, Ozempic, Wegovy and Mounjaro hold BPOM registrations. We found no BPOM registration for Rybelsus or Zepbound.

Brand Active ingredient BPOM status Source
Mounjaro Tirzepatide Approved February 2026 for type 2 diabetes; weight management added July 2026. Launched in Jakarta on 4 July 2026 by PT Anugerah Pharmindo Lestari BPOM announcement, 4 July 2026; RRI
Ozempic Semaglutide Registered, number DKI2164605043A1, valid to 3 September 2030 BPOM record
Wegovy Semaglutide Registered, number DKI2464605443A1, valid to 18 June 2029 BPOM record
Rybelsus Semaglutide No BPOM registration found
Zepbound Tirzepatide No BPOM registration found; Zepbound is the US weight-management brand

BPOM’s July 2026 announcement also confirms that semaglutide and liraglutide are approved in Indonesia as GLP-1 receptor agonists with similar uses. BPOM says every registered medicine passed a scientific evaluation against international standards and stays under safety monitoring after approval.

All of these are prescription medicines. To check a product yourself, search its registration number on BPOM’s official checker, cekbpom.pom.go.id. A BPOM number belongs to one specific product. Only a product carrying that number is the registered medicine.

How to tell which drug a product contains

The brand name alone can mislead. Three lines on the pack tell you what is really inside.

  1. Active ingredient. Look for the word semaglutide or tirzepatide. If neither appears, the product is neither drug, whatever it is called.
  2. Maker or registrant. Semaglutide brands come from Novo Nordisk; tirzepatide brands come from Eli Lilly. In Indonesia, the registrant named on the pack is the local company that holds the BPOM licence.
  3. BPOM number. Search it on cekbpom.pom.go.id. The record should show the same product name and active ingredient as the pack.

If a pen or vial is sold under a code or a nickname instead of a brand, it is not Ozempic, Wegovy, Mounjaro or Zepbound. Ask a doctor or pharmacist before using any product you cannot verify.

Frequently asked questions

Is Mounjaro the same as Ozempic?

No. Mounjaro is tirzepatide, made by Eli Lilly. Ozempic is semaglutide, made by Novo Nordisk. Both are weekly injections for type 2 diabetes, but tirzepatide acts on the GIP and GLP-1 receptors, while semaglutide acts on GLP-1 only.

Are Ozempic and Wegovy the same drug?

Yes, both contain semaglutide from Novo Nordisk. Ozempic is approved for type 2 diabetes. Wegovy is approved for weight management and goes up to a higher dose.

Does Ozempic contain tirzepatide?

No. Ozempic contains only semaglutide. The tirzepatide brands are Mounjaro and Zepbound.

Is Zepbound the same as Mounjaro?

They contain the same molecule, tirzepatide, from the same maker. Mounjaro was approved first for type 2 diabetes; Zepbound is the US brand for weight management. In Indonesia, Mounjaro itself carries both uses.

What is the difference between a GLP-1 drug and a GLP-1/GIP drug?

A GLP-1 drug, such as semaglutide, activates one incretin receptor. A GLP-1/GIP drug, such as tirzepatide, activates two. Both lower blood sugar and reduce appetite.

Is tirzepatide available in Indonesia?

Yes. BPOM approved tirzepatide, sold as Mounjaro, in February 2026 for type 2 diabetes and added weight management in July 2026. It is a prescription medicine.

Can I switch from Ozempic to Mounjaro?

Only with a doctor. The two are different molecules, so their doses do not convert one to one. A doctor decides whether to switch and how to start.
